content: Identity-based framing traces to Bem's self-perception theory (1972, solid, well-replicated) and to Bryan/Walton/Rogers/Dweck 2011 PNAS field experiments where 'be a voter' (noun) framing beat 'to vote' (verb) framing by 11-14 points in turnout. IMPORTANT: a later large replication (Gerber et al., PNAS 2016 / Cambridge Behavioural Public Policy) found NO significant effect of the same noun-vs-verb manipulation. James Clear's Atomic Habits popularization of identity-based habits is not itself a research contribution; the underlying self-perception mechanism is credible but the flagship applied effect (noun-framing) has a serious failed replication. Treat identity framing as theoretically motivated but empirically fragile at the level of specific phrasing tricks.
